title: Statistics - Lesson 6: Interpreting Box Plots Assessment
description: Assessment for interpreting and comparing box plots using center, spread, shape, outliers, and context.

questions.question: A box plot has minimum 8, Q1 = 12, median 17, Q3 = 25, and maximum 31. Which value is the median?
questions.explanation: The median is the middle landmark in the five-number summary, so it is 17.

questions.question: A box plot has Q1 = 42 and Q3 = 58. What is the IQR? Enter just the number.
A box plot has minimum 35 and maximum 92. What is the range? Enter just the number.
Section A has median 76 and Section B has median 81 on the same test. Which conclusion is supported?
options: Section A has the higher typical score.
Section B must have the smaller IQR.
Section A must have a right-skewed distribution.
Section B has the higher typical score.
questions.explanation: The median is used to compare typical values. Since 81 is greater than 76, Section B has the higher typical score.

questions.question: Which comparison best describes consistency?
options: The group with the larger maximum is always more consistent.
The group with the smaller IQR is more consistent in the middle 50%.
The group with the longer title is more consistent.
The group with the higher minimum always has the larger range.
questions.explanation: Consistency in the middle 50% is measured by IQR; smaller IQR means less spread.

questions.question: A box plot directly shows the mean of the data set.
questions.explanation: A standard box plot shows the five-number summary, including the median, but it does not directly show the mean.

questions.question: Team A has five-number summary 20, 30, 45, 55, 70. Team B has 18, 28, 45, 62, 90. Which statement is most accurate?
options: Team A has a higher median and greater spread.
Team B has a lower median and smaller spread.
The teams have the same range and same IQR.
The teams have the same median, but Team B has greater spread.
questions.explanation: Both medians are 45. Team B's IQR is 62 - 28 = 34 and range is 90 - 18 = 72, both larger than Team A's IQR 25 and range 50.

questions.question: Which situation is best described by a long right whisker?
options: All values are exactly equal.
Most values are lower or moderate, with some high values stretching the data upward.
The data has no maximum.
The median must be the largest value.
questions.explanation: A long right whisker means values on the high side are more spread out, suggesting a right tail.

questions.question: A larger range always means the middle 50% of the data is more spread out.
questions.explanation: Range uses only the minimum and maximum. The middle 50% is measured by IQR, which can be small even when the range is large.

questions.question: A student compares two box plots and says, "Group C is better because its maximum is highest." What is the main weakness?
options: The student used the median too much.
The student computed IQR before range.
The student mentioned context too clearly.
The student ignored median and spread.
questions.explanation: A maximum is only one value. A stronger comparison also considers typical value and variability.

questions.question: Group A has median 68 and IQR 10. Group B has median 68 and IQR 24. Compare the two groups in one or two sentences.
questions.correctAnswer: The groups have the same typical value because both medians are 68. Group A is more consistent in the middle 50% because its IQR is smaller.
questions.explanation: The comparison should mention equal medians and different spreads.

questions.question: A box plot of commute times has a long right whisker. What does that suggest in context?
questions.correctAnswer: It suggests that some commute times are much longer than the rest, so the distribution may be right-skewed.
questions.explanation: The right side represents higher commute times, and a long whisker shows those values are spread out.

questions.question: Two classes have these summaries: Class 1: min 55, Q1 70, median 78, Q3 86, max 94. Class 2: min 50, Q1 68, median 82, Q3 90, max 98. Which statement is supported?
options: Class 1 has the higher median and larger IQR.
Both classes have the same median and range.
Class 2 has the higher median and a slightly larger IQR.
Class 1 has no spread because its scores are high.
questions.explanation: Class 2's median is 82 compared with Class 1's 78. Class 2's IQR is 22, slightly larger than Class 1's IQR of 16.

questions.question: Why should an interpretation of a box plot include the real context, not only numbers?
questions.correctAnswer: Context explains what the median and spread describe, such as scores, time, distance, or cost, so the conclusion is meaningful.
questions.explanation: Statistics become useful when the values are connected to the situation being measured.

questions.question: A box plot marks one high value as a separate point beyond the right whisker. How should you mention it in a careful conclusion?
questions.correctAnswer: I should say there appears to be a high outlier or unusually high value, and I should avoid letting that one value represent the whole group.
questions.explanation: A separate point can indicate an outlier, but careful interpretation still considers median and IQR.
